reason: The text demonstrates a strict and well-defined hierarchy throughout. Authority clearly flows from King Josiah downward through specific channels: the king commands the scribe Shaphan, who works with the high priest Hilkiah, who delegates to secondary priests and other officials. The king stands on the platform as supreme authority, makes binding covenants, and issues direct commands to all subordinates. The text shows no suggestion that hierarchy is unimportant or discouraged; rather, it illustrates precise hierarchical organization with each person acting within their defined role and rank.
